data.title: Substrate recognition and transport mechanism of the human proton-coupled amino-acid transporter 1 (SLC36A1)
data.authors: Yin J; Yang M et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Cryo-EM structures of human PAT1 (SLC36A1) in apo and substrate-bound states reveal a convergent binding mode for diverse zwitterionic amino acids. This is a structural study; PAT1's role in lysosomal amino acid export and mTORC1 activation comes from earlier work.
data.abstract_excerpt: The proton-coupled amino-acid transporter SLC36A1 (hPAT1) is an atypical H+-driven carrier and mediates the intestinal absorption of a wide array of zwitterionic amino-acid analogs, including many compounds with central nervous-system (CNS) activity, as well as the activation of the mTORC1 pathway and the export of amino acids from lysosomes, thereby maintaining cellular amino-acid homeostasis.

extracted_findings.intervention: Structural/biochemical (cryo-EM of SLC36A1/PAT1, apo + 3 substrate-bound states)
extracted_findings.target: SLC36A1 (PAT1) / lysosomal amino acid efflux / mTORC1 activation
extracted_findings.species: Human (recombinant protein, cryo-EM; no animal/cell phenotype data)
extracted_findings.effect: Reveals the structural basis for the substrate promiscuity of PAT1; its role in lysosomal amino acid export and mTORC1 activation is prior work
